questions.prompt: With `Host.CreateDefaultBuilder(args)`, put the configuration sources in order from lowest to highest priority.
questions.explanation: Later sources override earlier ones: the base JSON file is overridden by the environment file, then user secrets, then environment variables, and command-line arguments have the highest priority.

questions.prompt: `appsettings.json` sets `App:Name` to `MyApp` and `App:MaxItems` to 50. `appsettings.Development.json` sets only `App:MaxItems` to 20. In Development, what values does the app see?
options: `Name` is missing and `MaxItems` is 20, because the environment file replaces the whole `App` section
`Name` is `MyApp` and `MaxItems` is 50, because `appsettings.json` wins
`Name` is `MyApp` and `MaxItems` is 20, because JSON keys merge and matching keys are overridden
The app fails to start, because the key is defined twice
questions.explanation: JSON keys merge; values in `appsettings.{ENV}.json` override `appsettings.json` only for matching keys, so `Name` keeps its default and `MaxItems` becomes 20.

questions.prompt: Do you need to rebuild the app to run it with a different `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` value?
options: Yes; the environment is compiled into the binaries
No; the environment is read when the app starts, so the same build only needs a restart
Yes, unless you delete the other `appsettings.*.json` files
No, and the app picks up the new value without a restart
questions.explanation: ASP.NET Core reads the environment at run time, at startup, not at build time. The same build can be deployed everywhere; only a restart is required after changing the variable.

questions.prompt: Which environment variable should a console or Worker app use to pick its environment?
options: `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`
`APPSETTINGS_ENVIRONMENT`
`DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT`
`HOST_ENVIRONMENT`
questions.explanation: The note lists `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` for ASP.NET Core web apps and `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` for console / Worker apps; using the wrong one is a common mistake.

options: `ConnectionStrings:Default`
`Default:ConnectionString`
`App:Default`
The environment variable `DEFAULT`
questions.explanation: `GetConnectionString("Default")` is the common pattern for reading `ConnectionStrings:Default`.

source.section: OPTION 2 — Manual ConfigurationBuilder (small tools or early bootstrap)

questions.prompt: What do you get from `new ConfigurationBuilder()...Build()` compared with `Host.CreateDefaultBuilder()`?
options: The same features, but with a shorter startup
Only `IConfiguration`; you must set up DI, logging, app lifetime and hosted services yourself
DI and logging, but no `appsettings.json` support
A full application host, including background services
questions.explanation: `ConfigurationBuilder` is a low-level, configuration-only builder: it gives `IConfiguration` but no DI, logging or lifetime management. `Host.CreateDefaultBuilder()` sets all of these up automatically.
